title: A top-up that costs a fee: what left and what arrived both kept (a and a2), the difference a spend on the fees line from Free to spend, and a transfer schedule with its fee (final_review_2 S4, decision Q2)
story: Set up Mon 4 Jan 2027 in pesos: the bank holds 20,000.00, of which 3,000.00 is what is left of Free to spend (typed), and an e-wallet holds nothing. Pay of 30,000.00 lands in the bank on the 25th (moved earlier) and starts the period; Free to spend is 5,000.00 a month. A top-up of 1,000.00 from the bank to the e-wallet is planned on the 5th and the 20th, and each one costs a 15.00 fee (the schedule carries `fee`). On Tue 5 Jan the check-in ticks the top-up: 1,015.00 left the bank and 1,000.00 arrived (a and a2). On Wed 6 Jan the bank statement is read: one line out of 1,015.00 on 5 Jan, which attaches to the transfer's bank side. Every amount is made up.

asks.question: bank_today
asks.why: 20,000.00 (opening) - 1,015.00 (top-up of Tue 5 Jan, what left the bank; the statement line attaches to it) = 18,985.00

asks.question: bank_today
asks.note: Before Q2 one currency left a2 out, so the e-wallet showed 1,015.00 when it held 1,000.00 (final_review_2 S4).

asks.question: safe_to_spend
asks.why: 18,985.00 (Bank today) - 1,015.00 (Top-up 20 Jan: 1,000.00 and its 15.00 fee, from the schedule's fee) = 17,970.00
asks.note: Its lowest point is 20 Jan; pay comes on Mon 25 Jan. Before Q2 the schedule had one amount for both sides and each top-up came off 15.00 short.

asks.question: headline
asks.why: 3,000.00 (Free to spend at the opening, typed) - 15.00 (the top-up's fee: a spend from the bank on the fees line, in Free to spend) = 2,985.00
asks.note: Free to spend caps the headline: the bank's 17,970.00 and the e-wallet's 1,000.00 are far above it.
